rationale: While earlier descriptions of Alsahan-Harris syndrome and TBC1D32-associated ciliopathies emphasized survivable pediatric phenotypes (e.g., hypothalamic/pituitary dysfunction, facial dysmorphism, polydactyly, retinal disease), subsequent cohort expansions report life-limiting prenatal presentations. Specifically, Harris et al. (2023) identified four fetal probands with life-limiting congenital anomalies among 14 total cases, and curation databases like PanelApp have reviewed TBC1D32 within cystic kidney disease panels. Consequently, while renal dysplasia and neonatal lethality are absent in classic mild/pediatric presentations, they cannot be reliably treated as absolute negative discriminators across the full TBC1D32 phenotypic spectrum.

evidence.text: Harris et al. describe seven newly identified probands with biallelic TBC1D32 variants, including four fetal probands from three unrelated pedigrees with life-limiting congenital anomalies, alongside three pediatric probands and comparisons to seven previously published individuals.

source.quote: We describe seven unpublished probands with rare likely pathogenic variants or variants of uncertain significance that segregate with recessive disease in TBC1D32, including four fetal probands in three unrelated pedigrees and three pediatric probands in unrelated pedigrees. We also report clinical comparisons with seven previously published patients... We provide additional data to expand the phenotype correlated with TBC1D32 variants, including a severe prenatal phenotype associated with life-limiting congenital anomalies.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and histological characterization of renal cystic dysplasia and pulmonary hypoplasia among prenatally ascertained TBC1D32 fetal cases?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether life-limiting fetal presentations feature true Meckel-Gruber-like multicystic renal disease or distinct developmental abnormalities is crucial for prenatal diagnostic algorithms.

new_directions.question_text: Do null/truncating bi-allelic TBC1D32 variants correlate with fetal lethality and renal phenotypes compared to hypomorphic missense variants seen in surviving pediatric Alsahan-Harris patients?
new_directions.rationale: Genotype-phenotype correlations across the reported 14+ patients may explain why severe life-limiting anomalies occur in some pedigrees while others survive into late childhood.
